chief_complaint: Uncontrolled hypertension and metabolic risk management
history_of_present_illness: The patient is a 57‑year‑old male with longstanding obesity, prediabetes, and stage 2 hypertension (SBP 140 mmHg). Recent vital signs show persistent elevated blood pressure. He has chronic anemia, ongoing psychosocial stressors including intimate partner violence, drug misuse, and housing insecurity. Despite multiple risk factors, he is only on inhaled asthma medications and has had very few outpatient visits in the past two years, indicating gaps in chronic disease management.
past_medical_history: Prior resolved conditions include recurrent viral sinusitis, multiple episodes of gingival disease and loose dental fillings, and prior medication review encounters. Dental imaging from 1983 to 2022 reflects chronic oral health issues. No documented chronic pulmonary disease beyond childhood asthma.

active_medications.name: Fluticasone propionate inhaler (Flovent)
active_medications.purpose: Maintenance therapy for asthma or reactive airway disease

social_determinants: Refugee status, housing insecurity, intimate partner violence, drug misuse, criminal record, full‑time employment, and prior higher education. These factors likely limit access to care, medication adherence, and healthy lifestyle options.
risk_factor_summary: Stage 2 hypertension (SBP 140/DBP 76), obesity (BMI ≥ 30), prediabetes (A1c 6.3%), chronic anemia, Charlson comorbidity index 1, moderate clinical complexity. No lipid panel, eGFR, or smoking data available. Elevated risk across cardiovascular, metabolic, hematologic, pulmonary, and psychosocial domains.

data_quality_flags.issue: BMI value missing; obesity is documented but exact BMI unavailable.
Renal function not recorded; CKD status unknown.
Lipid panel absent; ASCVD risk cannot be fully assessed.
No iron studies, B12/folate, or occult blood testing documented.
No antihypertensive agents prescribed despite stage 2 hypertension.
No metformin or other glucose‑lowering therapy despite prediabetes and obesity.
No statin or other lipid‑lowering therapy documented.
No antidepressant, anxiolytic, or PTSD‑related medication despite stress, IPV, and drug misuse.
No recent dental treatment or preventive care noted despite loss of teeth and chronic oral disease.

clinical_impression: The patient presents with high‑risk metabolic syndrome (obesity, hypertension, prediabetes) that is inadequately treated, compounded by chronic anemia and significant psychosocial stressors (IPV, drug misuse, housing insecurity). Limited pharmacologic therapy (only inhaled asthma agents) and missing key laboratory data suggest gaps in chronic disease management and opportunities for comprehensive cardiovascular, metabolic, renal, and mental health interventions.
